verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The Re_θ identity is present exactly: `core_radial_reynolds` gives (core velocity)·(radial length) = q^(-h), with ν normalized to 1 inside `reynolds` rather than appearing as a divisor (the paper's display keeps ν and fixes ν > 0 in the following line). Two parts of the display have no counterpart I found. (i) The divergence "⟶ ∞": `core_radial_reynolds` is an algebraic identity valid for every real h and every q > 0; it does not assert q^(-h) → ∞ as q ↓ 0, which needs h > 0. The general ingredient is present and is one instantiation away — `BlowupImplication.negative_power_tendsto_atTop` (BlowupImplication.lean:24) gives Tendsto (fun t => q t ^ (-A)) l atTop from 0 < A and q → 0⁺, so at A := h it yields the display's ⟶ ∞ — but I found no declaration that instantiates it at the Reynolds number. Grepping NavierStokes/ for the name gives five lines: the two concrete uses, `NaturalCore.lean:437` and `BaseResidual.lean:110`, both take A := CoordinateAlgebra.A h = 1/2 + h, the velocity exponent, not h; the other two (BlowupImplication.lean:44, 69) keep A abstract. (ii) Re_r := |u_r|ℓ_r/ν = O(1): no declaration was found. `Scaling.lean` defines no radial velocity scale q^(-1/2), and the one neighbouring theorem, `core_axial_reynolds`, pairs the core velocity with the axial length and yields q^(-2h), which is a different quantity, not Re_r. This display is not confined to Section 2's physical description. Searching the paper for "Reynolds"/"Re" returns exactly three places: here (p. 4), the proof outline on p. 8, which restates the whole display in the similarity variable — "Re_θ = q^{-A} ℓ_r = q^{-h} ⟶ ∞, Re_r = |u_r^{(0)}| ℓ_r = O(1)" — and p. 81, "the base velocity and radial length give Reynolds number of order q^{-h}". The clause that recurs in Lean-matching form is precisely the one the Lean supplies: `core_radial_reynolds` is the p. 8 identity verbatim (velocity q^{-A}, A h = 1/2 + h, times radialLength q = q^{1/2}, equals q^{-h}), and the atlas entry for `NavierStokes/Scaling.lean` places it with the §7 material at that page ("(7.2), p.81"). The two pieces with no counterpart found, the divergence and Re_r = O(1), recur only in that p. 8 outline restatement; I did not find either used as a formula inside a proof, and the severity is low on that basis rather than on the display being Section-2-only.
